column1: # AQL Language Specification: the aql:fmt module
# The source pretty-printer, exposed as a runtime API. Fmt.format formats
# AQL source text into canonical layout (normalised spacing, a trailing
# newline) and shares its implementation with the `aql fmt` CLI. The result
# is the formatted string, so the expected column is the canonical
# single-quoted rendering with the trailing newline shown as \n.
# The non-concrete-argument error arm is pinned by a Go test
# (lang/go/modules/fmt_test.go) rather than an ERROR row here.
import "aql:fmt" end Fmt.format "[ a  b  c ]"
column3: Fmt.format collapses list spacing and adds a trailing newline
Fmt.format normalises map spacing
Fmt.format keeps canonical source but ensures a trailing newline

column1: import "aql:fmt" end Fmt.format "def double fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x mul 2]]"
column3: Fmt.format drops brackets around a single fn param and return
Fmt.format keeps a minilang literal verbatim (its [ ] + delimiters are not re-tokenised) while normalising the surrounding spacing
Fmt.format leaves a pipe-delimited minilang literal untouched
Fmt.format keeps the lowercase none VALUE verbatim (never rewrites it to the None type)
Fmt.format keeps the list constructor word verbatim (never rewrites it to the List type)
Fmt.format still capitalises a genuine lowercase type name

column1: import "aql:fmt" end Fmt.format "def sum3 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer c:Integer] [Integer] [a add b add c]] end sum3 1 2 3"
column2: 'def sum3 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer c:Integer] [Integer] [a add b add c]]\n  end sum3 1 2 3\n'
column3: Fmt.format never drops statements that trail a fn definition (no truncation)
Fmt.format-markdown reformats a fenced aql block
Fmt.format-html reformats a marker region, leaving the rest
Fmt.render lays a doc flat when it fits the width
Fmt.render breaks a doc that does not fit the width

column1: # The XSLT-style rule vocabulary: Fmt.kind supplies a node's dispatch key
# (an XSLT match pattern) and Fmt.children its child sequence
# (apply-templates' node list). Both are pure value->value transforms, so a
# declarative rule table + a four-line apply driver — the whole formatter —
# is ordinary AQL (see the end-to-end loop in modules/fmtrule_test.go).

column3: Fmt.kind classifies an untagged Map as 'map'
Fmt.kind classifies a List as 'list'
Fmt.kind classifies a scalar leaf as 'scalar'
Fmt.kind reports a $kind-tagged Map's own tag
Fmt.children yields one entry node per Map key
Fmt.children yields a List's elements verbatim
Fmt.children yields no children for a scalar leaf

column3: Fmt.tree parses source into a $kind-tagged CST whose root node classifies as 'root'
Fmt.tree exposes each node's text and children, so a rule set can walk real AQL source

column1: # The declarative rule table: Fmt.rules exposes the canonical layout
# stylesheet as AQL data; Fmt.format-with formats under a (partial)
# override table. Rules are DATA and the emitter is the processor that
# interprets them (the XSLT split); whitespace — attachment, indent,
# width, fill-wrapping — is owned by the rules, which is why overriding
# them changes it and why the canonical table reproduces Fmt.format

column3: the canonical rule table carries the 72-column width as data
an empty override table formats with the canonical rules

column1: import "aql:fmt" end eq (Fmt.format-with (Fmt.rules) "a, b; c") (Fmt.format "a, b; c")
column3: the AQL rule table is AUTHORITATIVE: feeding Fmt.rules back reproduces Fmt.format

column1: import "aql:fmt" end Fmt.format-with {width:20} "[alpha bravo charlie delta]"
column3: width is a rule: 20 columns wraps the list with the greedy fill
attachment is a rule: detaching comma spaces it like any word
a TEMPLATE override: the literals around the apply/q recursion op are the list's brackets
the canonical list template — literals around the recursion op, the XSLT-template analogue
an unknown statement strategy is rejected, not silently ignored
a misspelled rule key is rejected (typo protection)
a non-integer width is rejected
